items.summary: Microsoft Research has open-sourced Agensh, a decentralized harness for large teams of coding agents that removes the central orchestrator common to most agent frameworks. Each worker independently claims sub-tasks via Gitea and Mattermost, shares findings on a shared board, verifies work against acceptance criteria, and merges into a common Git repo—running concurrently without a lead agent. On ProgramBench's five hardest tasks using GPT-5.6-sol at high reasoning effort, scaling from 1 to 8 agents added 1.37 points; the 5-task mean rose from 19.31% (1 agent) to 28.78% (128 agents). Speed also improved: on pandoc, 128 agents passed 30% at the 30-minute checkpoint versus 60 and 90 minutes for 32 and 8 agents. With GPT-6.1-sol, pandoc reached 79.59% with 32 agents—though these figures are not in the v1 paper.
items.title: Microsoft Research Open-Sources Agensh Multi-Agent Harness

items.summary: Japanese carmakers are accelerating vehicle development timelines to compete with faster-moving Chinese rivals, which build new models in under two years versus the four to five years typical for Japanese firms. Nissan targets a 40% reduction through shared platforms and expects part types cut by 70%. Toyota’s Area 35 project aims to improve plant floor space use by 35%, while Suzuki plans development times around two years and Mitsubishi up to three years by roughly 2030.
items.title: Japanese Automakers Shorten Model Development Times Amid Chinese Competition

items.summary: Singapore's Straits Times market column reports that the Japanese yen surged against both the US dollar and euro, reaching a one-year high on Oct 23 amid global flight to safety. Disappointing technology and AI earnings plus Middle East tensions boosted demand for safe-haven assets. The piece also covers strong Q3 results from S-REITs including Keppel DC REIT (DPU up 11.7% year on year) and FCT, SGX chief Loh Boon Chye's decision to step down in mid-July 2027, and plantation firms responding to SGX haze queries. Figures are drawn from company filings and market data reported during the week.
items.title: Yen Hits One-Year High as SGX Chief Announces Departure

items.summary: Cognition has released Devin Vulnerability Fixes, a free, open-source set of three agent skills under the MIT license that find and patch vulnerable PHP, Node.js and self-managed GitLab deployments. The plugin targets three critical remote code execution advisories: PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619), the October 2026 Node.js release covering 10 CVEs and self-managed GitLab bug CVE-2026-110264 rated CVSS 10.0. It runs in Devin and other coding agents that read SKILL.md files, following a five-step workflow of inventory, approval, verification, testing before and after, and one pull request per repository. Cognition packaged the remediation workflow it used internally; no published fix-rate benchmark exists, as results depend on test coverage.
items.title: Cognition Releases Open-Source Plugin for Critical RCE Vulnerabilities

items.summary: Syria is pursuing a broad energy-sector revival as part of post-conflict reconstruction, with the transitional government now controlling key assets including the Omar oil field and Tabiyeh gas complex. Wood Mackenzie figures indicate conflict-related output declines: oil production down 80 per cent and gas by half from pre-war levels of 380,000 bpd crude and 900 million cubic feet of gas. The government has signed deals with Chevron, Qatar’s UCC Holding, the Syrian Petroleum Company, ACWA Power, Marv Energy, and a $7 billion consortium to expand oil, gas, solar, wind, and hydropower capacity. Analysts note potential as an energy trade hub amid Strait of Hormuz restrictions, per the Baker Institute.
items.title: Syria Pursues Energy Sector Revival After Conflict Damage

items.summary: Vietnam’s government ordered provincial and municipal authorities to introduce support policies for households installing self-consumption rooftop solar systems by the end of December 2026, under Government Office Dispatch No. 10790/VPCP-CN dated Oct. 22. The Ministry of Industry and Trade must propose deployment targets with installation capacities and commissioning schedules, prioritizing northern provinces facing supply constraints. Vietnam Electricity reported 134,410 rooftop solar installations totaling more than 11.45 GW at the end of August 2026.
items.title: Vietnam Orders Provinces to Add Rooftop Solar Incentives by December 2026

items.summary: According to EnergySage's Home Electrification Marketplace Report, U.S. residential solar prices rose 3.2% in the first half of 2026 to a median $2.57/W, up from $2.49/W six months earlier. The increase followed the expiration of the federal tax credit and higher labor costs. Third-party ownership financing grew sharply as installers sought alternatives after the Section 25D credit ended in late 2025, with installer quotes for such products rising to about 41%. EnergySage cautioned that long-term savings from newer pre-paid offerings remain unestablished, and noted its findings reflect marketplace quotes rather than a full census of installations.
items.title: U.S. Residential Solar Prices Rise as Third-Party Ownership Grows

items.summary: Volkswagen is introducing the ID. Unyx 09 electric sedan in China, developed through its partnership with XPENG to compete against domestic EV makers amid industry struggles there. The car offers a CLTC range of 755 km (469 miles) and costs from 179,900 yuan ($26,939) for the Ultra version up to 249,900 yuan ($37,421) for the Max. It uses a VLA driving system from XPENG and an LFP battery from CATL.
items.title: Volkswagen Launches ID. Unyx 09 in China With XPENG Partnership

items.summary: A CleanTechnica author argues that the Trump administration's war on Iran has caused or revealed a seismic shift in global oil markets, making demand elastic for the first time. The piece notes EIA and IEA projections of over 2 million barrels per day decline in consumption by 2026, which would be unprecedented without an economic crisis. Analyzing gasoline prices above $4 adjusted for inflation across five historical periods, the author concludes high fuel costs did not reduce demand until 2026, suggesting price sensitivity has increased. The hypothesis remains untested and is offered openly for debate, with the author attributing accelerated transition to a post-oil world partly to Trump's policies.
items.title: CleanTechnica Author Proposes Oil Demand Is Becoming Elastic Amid Iran Conflict

items.summary: FIFA has formally opened a tender for the media rights to broadcast and stream the men's 2030 World Cup in the United States, with bids due by November 19. This is the first open sale of these U.S. rights since 2011. The tournament will be hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco, while FIFA also allows combined offers for the 2034 event in Saudi Arabia. Netflix, Disney and Amazon are among platforms reportedly interested.
items.title: FIFA Opens Bidding for US Rights to 2030 World Cup

items.summary: The item lists the winners of Emergent Ventures’ twentieth cohort in India, a group of engineers, students and self-taught builders who received grants for projects spanning manuscript digitization, AI assistants for shopkeepers, clinical tools for ADHD and cancer records, autonomous spacecraft technologies, air-water extraction machines, and regenerative-medicine biomaterials. Several recipients are teenagers or early-career researchers; one project aims to make graft designs 30–40% more affordable. The piece notes that unfamiliar readers can learn about Emergent Ventures through two links, directs them to the EV India announcement for this cohort’s details.
items.title: Emergent Ventures India awards grants to young founders and researchers

items.summary: SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk said on X that the Ukrainian military breached Starlink's terms of service by using the satellite network to conduct offensive drone strikes. He stated that this loophole was closed last week and clarified that the civilian service was never intended for such use, while noting that the separate military-grade system Starshield remains under U.S. government control.
items.title: Musk Says Ukraine Violated Starlink Terms for Drone Strikes

items.summary: The UK government announced that more than £1bn would be provided in the upcoming Budget for social and affordable housing in England, pushing total funding for its 10-year homes programme past £40bn. Mayors and regional leaders are expected to receive greater powers, transitional seed funding of an initial £285m next year, and a new £1.5bn borrowing facility from 2028. Chancellor John Healey said cities would get the right to decide their own future. Separately, reports suggest billions in defence spending may be unveiled, prompting shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith to call for Healey's resignation over plans to reach 3% of GDP on defence by 2030.
items.title: Healey's Budget to Fund £1bn for Social and Affordable Housing

items.summary: A Guardian review of freedom-of-information data found that most UK levelling up projects are still not finished, years after funds were allocated. Of 1,347 funded projects examined, 821 remained unfinalised as of May this year, and 73 council areas had completed none at all. Jack Shaw of Groundwork Research said the figures reveal a large gap between ambition and delivery. Zoë Billingham of IPPR North criticised short-term funding pots, while Sarah Longlands warned Labour's Pride in Place programme could face similar delays. The government responded that long-term targeted funding would support local communities.
items.title: UK levelling up projects remain largely unfinished years after funding

items.summary: The UK government has launched the pride in place programme, allocating £20m to North East Lincolnshire council for regeneration of its struggling town centre. Residents report visible improvements, including a new cinema and community spaces, yet many remain doubtful about whether funding will meaningfully address deep-rooted decline driven by online shopping, industrial collapse and out-of-town retail parks. Neela Parker Talwar of the Centre for Cities argues that £20m is not so much money and cannot fund major projects like buying large empty buildings. She warns that causes such as access to jobs may lie beyond local authority reach. Some residents instead place their hope in a stronger local economy rather than government schemes.
items.title: Pride in Place scheme faces scepticism over Grimsby's high street revival

items.summary: The 19th EU-China Business and Technology Cooperation Fair concluded in Chengdu on October 23, drawing representatives from nearly 700 companies and institutions across more than 20 countries for face-to-face discussions. New energy, environmental protection, and intelligent robotics were among the key sectors highlighted as participants explored opportunities between European businesses and China.
items.title: 19th EU-China Fair Concludes in Chengdu With Nearly 700 Attendees

items.summary: Senior UN officials marked the 55th anniversary of China's restoration to its lawful United Nations seat by reaffirming their adherence to General Assembly Resolution 2758. Guy Ryder, UN under-secretary-general for policy, told CGTN that the organization continues to be guided by and will uphold the resolution consistently. Stephen Jackson, UN resident coordinator in China, called it a historic moment that eliminated possibilities of two Chinas or Taiwan independence and strengthened Global South representation on the Security Council. Adopted October 25, 1971 with an overwhelming majority at the UNGA's 26th session, the resolution restored all rights of the People's Republic of China.
items.title: UN officials reaffirm Resolution 2758 as China's seat turns 55

items.summary: The number of China-Europe freight train trips through the network's eastern corridor reached a record high this year, as goods increasingly shifted toward higher-value technology-intensive products. As of Friday, the corridor had handled 6,024 trips this year, up 40.3% year on year, marking the first time annual traffic surpassed 6,000 trips.
items.title: China-Europe freight trains hit record high on eastern corridor

items.summary: At the 29th Beijing Music Festival, director Zou Shuang presents The Magic Flute in an unexpected new setting. CGTN went beyond the stage to meet the international cast and creative team behind the production. They discussed the surprises shaping the staging and how modern Beijing is influencing their experience of Mozart's timeless opera.
items.title: Beijing Stages Mozart's Magic Flute With Modern Chinese Setting

items.summary: President Donald Trump defended his use of tariffs at a campaign rally in Georgia, saying they have made the U.S. richer and that Volkswagen agreed to build a new $4.2 billion Audi plant there. He called it 'the single largest investment in U.S. auto industry history' and said without tariffs, companies would not be coming.
items.title: Trump Defends Tariffs as Audi Announces U.S. Plant

items.summary: The People's Action Party elected its next central executive committee at a conference on Oct 25, with cadres voting from a secret ballot of 19 candidates. First-term ministers Jeffrey Siow and Jasmin Lau were placed on the nomination list but were not voted in. Secretary-General Lawrence Wong said the party must earn continued support rather than rely on past mandates, warning that younger Singaporeans may feel less bond unless connected to them on their own terms.
items.title: PAP elects new central executive committee; Siow and Lau nominated but not voted in

items.summary: The Diamonds lead Australia's live blog opens with Australia trailing New Zealand 2-0 in game three of the Constellation Cup in Sydney. Coach Stacey Marinkovich says her team must win the first five minutes and play more disciplined netball after being penalised heavily, conceding 145 penalties to New Zealand's 100.
items.title: Australia trail New Zealand two games into Constellation Cup

items.summary: A three-day chase in the Tochigi capital of Utsunomiya ended when a zookeeper shot a bear with a tranquilizer gun near a private residence, an episode widely shown on TV and online. The incident is seen as part of a growing number of human–bear conflicts across Japan following last fiscal year’s record 238 attacks and 13 deaths nationwide. Experts warn of another pre-hibernation surge this fall but note rich acorn harvests may keep many bears well fed, likely limiting the worst outcomes.
items.title: Japan braces for more bear attacks after Utsunomiya hunt

items.summary: Nearly 1,000 arrests were made as hundreds of thousands protested across France on Saturday before some clashes late in the day, officials said. Police fired tear gas and water cannon to disperse demonstrators in cities including Paris, while barricades burned in Marseille and a shop was ransacked in Bordeaux. Officials avoided rioting and looting at last weekend's scale. The interior ministry put Saturday's turnout at an estimated 410,000; unions said about 800,000. Some 70,000 police were deployed amid restrictions over cost-of-living and school grievances. President Macron had limited demonstrations to those led by recognised unions. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez reported several thousand radical activists gathered at the march's rear, including around 500 identified as rioters, while nearly 1,000 arrests would rise further. Two people were seriously injured in Toulouse and Clermont-Ferrand.
items.title: France Arrests Nearly 1,000 After Mass Protests Turn Violent

items.summary: Australia’s federal police commissioner, Krissy Barrett, says politicians’ rhetoric is fuelling threats and abuse against leaders after MP Helen Haines was allegedly deliberately attacked outside her Wangaratta office. She remains serious but stable at the Alfred hospital following a double leg amputation. Barrett reports that threat summaries once read “pages and pages long,” links physical hate mail to online threats, and says she would challenge anyone calling such abuse free speech.
items.title: AFP Commissioner Links Political Rhetoric to Surge in Threats Against MPs

items.summary: A man has died following a workplace incident on a rural property near Shepparton in Victoria's north-east. Emergency services were called to Evans Road, Waggarandall, about 40 kilometres north-east of Shepparton, where the man was reported trapped under a loading ramp around 10:20am on Sunday. Advanced life support paramedics attended but he died at the scene. Police and SES also responded; police will report to the coroner.
items.title: Man dies after being crushed by ramp in northern Victoria

items.summary: Manila police are investigating a laptop and child abuse images found in the former home of Meghan Markle's estranged father, Thomas Markle. Interior minister Jonvic Remulla told AFP that forensic results would arrive within a week and that appropriate legal action could follow if evidence is sufficient; Markle denies all claims. British tabloid the Sun first reported it.
items.title: Philippines Investigates Laptop Found at Thomas Markle's Former Home

items.summary: Kim Aris, son of Aung San Suu Kyi, said after an eight-year-gap phone call that his 81-year-old mother appears mentally and physically well yet lives in near-complete isolation. He described her as effectively held in solitary confinement with no contact beyond military or police figures, and uncertain whether she is located at a fenced residence in Naypyidaw. Aris characterised recent government photographs of her as public-relations stunts rather than evidence of fair treatment. He said international support for her has dwindled since the 2016-2017 Rohingya crisis and that she remains shut off from news, though he noted her past statements on the issue could fill volumes. The article places this within Myanmar's 2021 military coup and a civil war that conflict monitors say has killed more than 100,000 people.
items.title: Suu Kyi's son says she is healthy but isolated

items.summary: Police clashed with protesters in Paris after a largely peaceful day of demonstrations turned violent on Saturday night, as crowds threw objects and fireworks at officers. Around 70,000 police were deployed across France for a second consecutive weekend, using tear gas and water cannons to disperse crowds. The Interior Ministry estimated around 400,000 people took part in Saturday's demonstrations, with nearly 1,000 arrests made.
items.title: Protesters and Police Clash in Paris After Nightfall Unrest

items.summary: On the last day of campaigning, Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro held their closing rallies on Saturday in Rio de Janeiro, one day after a combative final television debate. Opinion polls show them neck and neck, with around 20% of voters having abstained in the first round, where Bolsonaro won 47% over Lula's 45%. After three weeks of intense campaigning, the incumbent appears to have regained ground from his low approval rating of 24%, while Bolsonaro faces scrutiny over a bribery admission and ongoing investigations.
items.title: Brazilian candidates hold final rallies before runoff election

items.summary: Ukraine said Saturday that its Starlink satellite system and military's Starshield were back to high operating speeds after more than a week of disruptions. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy attributed the restoration to direct dialogue, while Ukrainian officials believe U.S. government pressure caused the earlier restrictions. Defense Minister Yevhen Khmara noted connectivity now exceeds 250 mph, up from about 100 mph during the outage.
items.title: Ukraine Reports Starlink and Starshield Speeds Restored

items.summary: Days before Israel's election, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced a major military operation in the West Bank city of Hebron after two soldiers were killed and three wounded at a checkpoint. The Israeli military said it was searching for militants and weapons near Friday's attack site. Local officials estimate around 250 families have been displaced, though Governor Khaled Dudin put the number lower at 150.
items.title: Netanyahu Orders Large-Scale Hebron Evictions After Soldier Deaths

items.summary: Rupert Lowe, leader of Britain's far-right Restore Britain party, said Saturday the UK owes no country 'unconditional' support after a report that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered backing for Argentina in its sovereignty dispute over the Falkland Islands. Lowe wrote on X that British interests should guide foreign policy alone and added the islands will remain British.
items.title: Restore Britain Leader Questions Unconditional Support for Israel

items.summary: The Metropolitan Police confirmed it received a letter in January 2019 containing claims about alleged offending outside the UK, but did not share details with other agencies. The force is considering referring itself to the Independent Office for Police Conduct over its handling. Meghan said she was deeply distressed by allegations concerning her father Thomas Markle; he denies possessing images and remains under investigation in the Philippines.
items.title: Met Police Confirm Receipt of Allegations Against Thomas Markle

items.summary: European student protests have spread across Europe, and in Serbia they are channeling the movement into Sunday's parliamentary elections through a list of candidates drawn from academics, economists, athletes and engineers rather than career politicians. The Student List positions itself as the most serious challenge yet to Aleksandar Vucic, who has led since 2012 after taking power following the Novi Sad railway station canopy collapse that killed sixteen people two years ago. Around 150,000 attended a recent rally in Belgrade's Slavija Square. Analysts note Vucic remains defiant and accused of dominating media through state resources, but observers say the election now looks uncertain for the first time in 14 years.
items.title: Serbian Students Turn Protests Into Election Challenge

items.summary: Nicole Sanchotene, project coordinator at NetLab (UFRJ), told Global Voices that big tech companies’ transparency and cooperation policies during Brazil’s 2026 election amount to ‘governance washing.’ She says platforms like Kwai—over 60 million users—and Meta do not fully comply with electoral norms. Users report sudden drops in Instagram Stories views after political posts; journalist Leandro Demori showed his fell from about one million or 400,000 views to 9,000 (s34). On October 16, Meta admitted technical problems affecting pro-Lula content delivery but denied bias, citing ‘global technical glitches’ and anti-fraud measures (s4,s3). Lula filed a complaint; the electoral court ordered equal treatment. Sanchotene stresses algorithms are opaque black boxes with no oversight, and that candidates may be running under unequal conditions—a global issue repeated across elections.
items.title: Brazilian Expert Calls Big Tech Transparency Policies 'Governance Washing'

items.summary: According to a Fortune report, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and his wife Priscilla Chan are shifting their philanthropic and corporate investments toward artificial intelligence, science and STEM education. The couple led $50 million to Sacramento State University for state-of-the-art STEM labs and an AI center, announced by California Governor Gavin Newsom on January 28 as part of a redevelopment plan turning three vacant Capitol Mall office buildings into a downtown campus. Zuckerberg said the investments would strengthen communities and support future leaders; Newsom added that students need affordable housing near where they study. The gift reflects a broader change at the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, which is directing most resources toward biomedical AI research through its Biohub network. CZI also laid off around 70 employees earlier this year as it streamlined operations.
items.title: Zuckerberg and Chan redirect giving toward AI and science

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to visit Uttar Pradesh and Odisha on Sunday, October 25. In Varanasi he will inaugurate a garment manufacturing facility at around 11 a.m., witness the Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026 as Chief Guest, and later travel to Bhubaneswar to inaugurate the RBI's Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute.
items.title: Modi To Visit Varanasi And Bhubaneswar On October 25

items.summary: Ukraine says Starshield and Starlink are back to full speed after a week-long slowdown that left its defences exposed, with Zelenskyy confirming restoration overnight. Ukraine's defence ministry reported stable speeds over 400 kph. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk accused the Ukrainian military of violating terms by using it for offensive strikes. Beskrestnov said long-range drone use remains physically impossible at 70-90 kph.
items.title: Ukraine Restores Starlink Speeds; Musk Blames Kyiv

items.summary: Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw assured support for projects transforming Andhra Pradesh into a global semiconductor design hub, announced during Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu’s Saturday courtesy call in Delhi. Vaishnaw said the Centre would back research and development, skill training and capacity building, plus AI infrastructure. The two also discussed railway connectivity proposals.
items.title: Railways Minister Assures Andhra Pradesh Semiconductor Support

items.summary: The Federation of LPG Distributors of India (FLDI) has urged its members to continue supply and delivery operations in Delhi, opposing calls for protests and an indefinite strike. The FLDI said the concerns of distributors are being heard and that it had received assurances of an early resolution as Rahul Gandhi’s INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1 raises disruption worries.
items.title: LPG distributor body urges members to keep supplying ahead of Gandhi rally

items.summary: The CBI registered an FIR against M/s IL&FS Energy Development Company Ltd and its top executives on Oct 21, following a complaint from Canara Bank’s Bandra circle office. Searches across Delhi, Mumbai and Noida seized incriminating documents. According to the CBI, the accused allegedly conspired to obtain a Rs 100 crore term loan and $50 million foreign currency loan, diverting funds through associate entities and causing an estimated wrongful loss of Rs 212.3 crore via conspiracy and cheating charges.
items.title: CBI files FIR against IL&FS Energy, top execs in Rs 212cr Canara Bank loan fraud case

items.summary: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement has taken into custody Himanshu Bhau and Neeraj Kaushik at the Henderson Detention Centre in Nevada. According to Haryana Police, Bhau entered the US using a forged passport surname after fleeing India amid murder and extortion charges; discrepancies in his biometric data led investigators to identify him as wanted criminals. His criminal network is linked to several shootings across India. He faces deportation through cooperation with the CBI. The report also includes an unrelated profile of journalist Bobins at Live Mint.
items.title: ICE Detains Two Indian Gangsters in Las Vegas

items.summary: The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority warned residents to stay alert as a depression over the east-central and southeast Bay of Bengal is expected to strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by October 27. Managing Director Prakhar Jain cautioned against lowering guard, while the Meteorological Department projected further intensification toward a very severe cyclonic storm near the Andhra Pradesh coast around October 28.
items.title: Andhra Pradesh braces for intensifying Bay of Bengal depression

items.summary: At the inaugural Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship 2026 in Ahmedabad, India's men beat Uganda 44-30 and its women crushed Singapore 32-16 on Saturday. Shivam Patare led the raiding effort with eight points; Sakshi topped the women's attack with six. The victories highlighted balanced Indian raid and defence as teams prepare for Sunday matches against Uganda and Malaysia, per a press release auto-generated by an agency feed.
items.title: India Clinch Double Victory at Inaugural Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship

items.summary: The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) alleged that slogans including “Free Umar Khalid” and “Long Live Naxalbari” were written on the walls of Delhi's Jawaharlal Nehru University, urging action against those responsible. The claims came two days after similar slogans were reportedly spotted at Jamia Millia Islamia University in the capital. ABVP JNU said the administration should identify offenders and take appropriate action to safeguard the campus atmosphere. The JNU administration has reportedly taken cognisance of the matter and is looking into it, saying it would not allow vested interests to disturb peace on the campus. Congress leader Imran Masood dismissed reports of “Free Kashmir” slogans at Jamia as fake news but acknowledged some posters carrying the slogan had been put up there. Tensions flared between teaching staff and students over disciplinary action amid ongoing protests about the restoration of the students' union, prompting the university to shift classes online.
items.title: ABVP Alleges Anti-India Slogans on JNU Walls and Demands Action

items.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Congress alleges that during a special voter campaign, block-level officers filled and pre-filled Form 8 for voters whose details differed from their EPIC cards. The party says the discrepancies appeared after April's Special Intensive Revision list was released, making it the Election Commission's responsibility to correct them rather than burdening voters. Whistleblower Kumud Gangwar said forms were signed without acknowledgment slips or dates. Anas Khan accused EC staff of using Form 8 receipts to blame voters and cover up alleged vote theft.
items.title: UP Congress Alleges EC Used Form-8 To Cover Up Voter Discrepancies

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is in Varanasi as the Indian Air Force marks its 94th Foundation Day with the finale of the 'Wings Over Ganges' air show at Namo Ghat. The display features Tejas, Rafale and Su-30 jets along with transport aircraft and helicopters. A Surya Kiran aerobatic team and Sarang display team are set to perform over the river Ganga during a 90-minute flypast watched by more than 12,000 spectators.
items.title: Modi Opens IAF Air Show in Varanasi

items.summary: A 25-year-old woman, seven months pregnant with twins and a resident of Utnoor, died on Saturday morning after being admitted to Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS) in Adilabad. Her family alleged the staff neglected her worsening condition before she died from pulmonary embolism at 32 weeks of pregnancy. RIMS director Dr Rathod JaiSingh said a three-member committee would investigate.
items.title: Family Alleges Negligence After Pregnant Woman Dies at RIMS

items.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party alleged that a Congress worker named Shilpa voted under the name of Asha Patil during Karnataka's Haveri MLC elections, claiming she entered the booth with Minister Rudrappa Lamani. BJP MLA Mahesh Tenginkai shared video evidence and demanded legal action. Congress spokesperson Shripad Renu dismissed the claims as baseless fairy tales spun by the opposition.
items.title: BJP and Congress Clash Over Alleged Fake Voting in Karnataka Haveri MLC Polls

items.summary: KL Rahul scored just four runs across two innings for India A, who were bowled out for 113 before New Zealand A posted 317 to take a 204-run lead. In the second innings he was dismissed hit-wicket after edging a ball toward himself and striking his own off stump with his bat while trying to stop it; replays showed the wicket would not have fallen anyway. Fraser Sheat took both of Rahul's dismissals.
items.title: KL Rahul dismissed twice in India A loss

items.summary: In an exclusive interview with PTI, Air Chief Marshal Singh said the guiding principle for India's theatreisation should be 'centralised control' where necessary and 'decentralised execution' where appropriate. He cited ongoing conflicts worldwide to assert that air power can decisively shape military outcomes, quoting himself: 'Recent conflicts around the world have once again underlined how decisively air power can shape military outcomes.' Singh said transformation of this scale should be implemented in phases so operational readiness is never compromised, and warned against predicting future battlefields with excessive certainty. He noted progress has stalled due to divergent views among services over command structures.
items.title: IAF chief outlines guiding principles for theatreisation

items.summary: AMMK General Secretary TTV Dhinakaran attacked the ruling Tamil Nadu government over soaring prices of essential commodities, warning that steep rice price increases could threaten the TVK government. He called it a “disaster” for voters and predicted its end soon. Quoting supporters, he said they united under Edappadi K Palaniswami to restore J Jayalalithaa’s Amma government to safeguard law and order.
items.title: Dhinakaran Warns Rising Rice Prices Could Threaten TVK Government

items.summary: Police in Fort Kochi registered a case against right-wing influencer Amrit Singh Darren over a video making communal allegations about the city, Kashi Art Café, and Kerala's Muslim community. The Ernakulam district committee of the Muslim Youth League lodged a complaint seeking stringent action, while the Democratic Youth Federation of India also condemned the remarks. Chief Minister VD Satheesan said attempts to divide communities would not be tolerated, and opposition leader Pinarayi Vijayan accused the Sangh Parivar of outsourcing hate through online provocateurs.
items.title: Kochi hate video prompts police case and political condemnations

items.summary: Young Indian protesters in Delhi have drawn on historical freedom struggles, notably the Quit India Movement of 1942 and events from 1919 and 1928, to frame their opposition to police actions during demonstrations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Students such as Devyani Sarkar, Neha Bora, Kriti Gupta, Annapurna, and Shubhit Kumar compared current repression—detentions of students and Opposition leaders—to British colonial rule, with one protester invoking Bhagat Singh’s line about replacing “white” colonizers with “black” ones. Comedian Shamik Chakrabarti dubbed Imran Khan’s expulsion from India ‘Quit India Movement 2’, while the Cockroach Janta Party timed a Mumbai protest to Gandhi’s birth anniversary and framed it as a mass jail campaign. The article presents these comparisons as symbolic resonance, not verified claims of government intent.
items.title: Indian protesters invoke colonial-era movements amid Delhi unrest

items.summary: A purported audio recording alleging a Rs 500-crore payment to Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange has ignited one of Maharashtra’s biggest political controversies, exposing tensions within the ruling Mahayuti alliance. The row began after Jarange released the recording and denied receiving any money, claiming it exposed a conspiracy against him. Allegations that funds were routed through Shiv Sena MP Shrikant Shinde drew sharp responses: BJP officials called it fake and AI-generated, while Shiv Sena leaders accused Jarange of colluding with BJP elements to target Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis ordered a forensic investigation into the clip’s authenticity and origins.
items.title: Maharashtra leaders clash over disputed Rs 500-crore audio clip

items.summary: The Kargil Democratic Alliance rejected the Union government’s October 15 draft governance framework for Ladakh, reported by The New Indian Express, saying it gives overriding authority to the lieutenant governor and bureaucracy while leaving little power with the proposed elected body. Talks have stalled after a May meeting; co-convener Asgar Karbalai said an earlier agreement had promised legislative, executive and financial powers plus Article 371-K safeguards, but the draft instead places governance under Article 240. Co-convener Sajjad Kargili called it “an attack on the rights of the people of this region.” The alliance warned of protests if agreed terms are not implemented.
items.title: Ladakh Leaders Reject Draft Governance Framework Over L-G Powers

items.summary: Audi plans a roughly $4.2 billion investment in Macon, Georgia, creating about 4,500 jobs with capacity for up to 200,000 vehicles annually and production targeted for the early 2030s, Audi said. Chairman Gernot Döllner announced it alongside Trump at a Perry rally, where he called it proof his trade policy draws manufacturing home. The move arrives amid competitive Georgia Senate and governor races ahead of midterm elections.
items.title: Audi's Georgia Plant Investment Becomes Trump Campaign Symbol

items.summary: A newsletter opens by explaining that humans prefer right angles through a trait called grid sensitivity, citing researcher Dinesh Katre and the Harappans' 4,000-year-old cities. It then turns to a heist in California where thieves broke into a FedEx truck outside Professional Sports Authenticator (PSA) and stole graded Pokémon cards worth around $963,000. The piece traces rising card prices through nostalgia, the pandemic, and speculation—mentioning Logan Paul's Pikachu flip from over $5 million to $16.5 million—and notes PSA deactivated the stolen cards' certification numbers after the robbery. It closes with a reader-recommended book by Jeet Thayil.
items.title: Why thieves target graded Pokémon cards, and why rectangles rule

items.summary: BJP leaders on Friday condemned National Conference president Farooq Abdullah after his reported remarks questioned India's intentions toward Kashmir and suggested Pakistan was pressuring New Delhi by raising the issue internationally. Sat Sharma demanded an apology, while Arjun Munda called the comments condemnable and Amar Kumar Bauri defended Centre policies citing development initiatives following the abrogation of Articles 370 and 35A.
items.title: BJP Leaders Condemn Farooq Abdullah Over Kashmir Remarks

items.summary: The Janata Dal (United), or JD(U), expelled Mokama MLA Anant Kumar Singh and his wife Neelam Devi for six years on Saturday, citing alleged anti-party activities, indiscipline and campaigning against the party's candidate in the Bihar Legislative Council elections. In an order issued by president Umesh Singh Kushwaha, the party cancelled both leaders' primary memberships and recommended that the Assembly Speaker cancel Singh's membership under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution. The couple had backed a Jan Suraaj Party candidate over JD(U)'s nominee Neeraj Kumar Singh. Expulsion from the party is separate from any disqualification process. Singh, who returned to the JD(U) for the 2025 Assembly election, has declared 28 criminal cases in his affidavit. items.title: JD(U) Expels Singh and Wife Over Election Row
